decisions.rationale: A change to the guardrails, the release trust or the delivery gate must name the checks it has to pass
Security decisions are kept as fingerprinted records and releases carry their evidence files
The guardrails, the signature checks and the gate are security behavior with test suites
Every lesson entry states the mechanism behind what broke
security findings groups findings by cause into the backlog
A lesson is closed only by a check that now enforces it
The runtime and hooks start commands from repository and hook input
The repository is public and sits beside signing keys and client checkouts
No third-party runtime package; Node, git and two pinned CI actions are the components
Skilliton has no sign-in of its own; it runs as the local user and git and gh do the signing
There is no server and no session token for Skilliton to issue or check
The shared-repository gate decides who may change the policy, by signature
Hook input, configuration, records and manifests are untrusted text reaching parsers, paths and commands
Guardrail blocks, holds and gate rejections must leave a readable record
Policy and CI changes need an approver's signature where the gate is installed
